severity.title: Three Severity Levels
severity.description: Issues are categorised as errors (must fix), warnings (should review), and suggestions (optional improvements).

oneClick.title: One-Click Fixes
oneClick.description: Each issue shows the exact before → after change. Apply it instantly or skip it — you stay in control.

fullText.title: Full Corrected Text
fullText.description: A clean corrected version is generated alongside the issue list so you can copy it directly without applying fixes one by one.

items.emails: Polishing professional emails before sending to clients or executives
items.essays: Proofreading essays, cover letters, and academic submissions
items.nonNative: Non-native English speakers checking grammar before publishing
items.bloggers: Bloggers doing a final pass before hitting publish
items.teams: Teams reviewing shared documents for consistency and correctness

items.writeFirst: Write first, check grammar after — editing as you type disrupts flow and produces worse writing.
items.review: Review suggestions carefully; stylistic recommendations may not always fit your intended voice.
items.twice: Run it twice: once after writing, once after making your own edits.
items.sections: For long documents, paste in sections to get more focused, accurate feedback.

kinds.question: What kinds of issues does it find?
kinds.answer: Three types: errors (grammar and spelling mistakes), warnings (likely problems such as awkward agreement or punctuation), and suggestions (optional style and clarity improvements).

apply.question: How do I apply the fixes?
apply.answer: Each issue comes with a suggested replacement. You can review issues one by one or copy the fully corrected text — you stay in control of which changes to accept.

location.question: How do I know where each issue is in my text?
location.answer: Every issue includes its exact character position, so it can be located and highlighted in your original text rather than just listed abstractly.

style.question: Does it rewrite my style?
style.answer: No. It focuses on correctness — grammar, spelling, and punctuation — plus optional clarity suggestions. If you want a full rewrite, use the Paraphraser instead.

cost.question: How much does a check cost?
cost.answer: Token cost scales with text length at roughly 1 text token per 6 characters. If the check fails, the tokens are refunded automatically.
